question: None shared. P-117 (Aljalal et al. 2024; correct file downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1746809423008959-main.pdf) is a binary amnestic MCI vs healthy control classification from resting-state EEG. P-95 is a three-class AD/MCI/control classification from 482 neuropsychological and neuroradiological (MRI) attributes, and it reports no binary MCI-vs-control result. The comparison differs (three-class against binary), and so does the channel (clinical/cognitive tests plus MRI against EEG).
metric: Both are accuracies, but of different estimands: a three-class accuracy (chance 33%) against a binary accuracy (chance about 50%).

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy, aMCI vs HC, 10-fold CV over 3660 EEG segments from 61 participants. Wilson with n = 61: centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06298 = 0.9686; half-width 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].
figures.P-95: Three-class accuracy with all attributes, 66.22% to 81.00% across seven classifiers (weighted AUROC 76.3% to 95.0%); 90 participants (30 AD, 30 MCI, 30 controls), 10-fold stratified CV. Wilson with n = 90: 81.00% gives [0.717, 0.878]; 66.22% gives [0.560, 0.752].

matched_figure_check: None exists. P-95 gives no binary MCI-vs-control figure and P-117 gives no three-class figure, so neither paper reports the other's condition.
performance_validity: The Section 3.5 exclusion applies to P-117 on its own source: 99.81% from internal 10-fold CV over randomly split segments of 61 participants, with no external cohort. P-95 (at most 81%) is not near ceiling.
reason: P-95's 66-81% is a three-class AD/MCI/control accuracy from neuropsychological and MRI attributes. P-117's 99.81% is a binary aMCI-vs-control accuracy from EEG. Task, comparison and channel all differ (condition 1). P-117's figure also meets the near-ceiling exclusion on its own PDF (condition 5). No shared quantity exists, so no difference beyond uncertainty can be established.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.
Results: The accuracy for the whole set of attributes ranged between 66.22 % and 81.00 %, and the weighted average AUROC was between 76.3 % and 95.0 %.
The output attribute is Class, which holds one of the three values (AD, MCI or C) and it is the target for classification algorithms.
As the dataset contains exactly 30 representatives of each of the three classes (AD, MCI, C) and since the experiments are based on 10-fold stratified cross-validation
